expectation: Membrane rings on most T cells and NK cells: small round lymphocytes, common in immune-rich stroma. They should sit as scattered single cells and dense aggregates in stroma and infiltrates, and be sparse inside tumour nests.
observed: A: distinct yellow cells, dense in some ROIs and in stromal bands, sparse in others; density differs by ROI and does not follow the nuclear stain. B/C: a few discrete small cells, some ring-like, at the edges of nests. D: a cluster of ring-stained cells.
why: Discrete small cells with membrane staining gather in stroma and aggregates and vary by ROI independently of nuclear density, which is the pattern of T and NK cells.
notes: CD7 marks scattered and clustered small cells with membrane rings. They are dense in immune-rich stromal ROIs and sparse in nests, a lymphocyte pattern rather than haze or debris.
